name: reaction-lead-on
context: Corvin and the player are in the hall. The adjacent parlour is open and accessible.
player: Come to the parlour with me.
reason: Indirect assent creates an expectation of following now.

name: reaction-future-promise
context: Corvin can speak at tomorrow's council meeting.
player: Will you speak for me at tomorrow's council?
reply: Tomorrow, when the council convenes, I will speak on your behalf.
reason: Record a triggered future obligation, not an immediate action.

name: reaction-general-support
context: Corvin has not previously offered support. No specific plan or political proposal has been discussed.
player: Can I count on your help?
reason: Broad support matters but must not become an invented task.

name: reaction-gift
context: Corvin holds a brass key and may give it away. The player is beside him.
reply: Certainly. *I hand you the brass key.*
reason: The GM should resolve a narrated handover against actual inventory.

name: reaction-refused-trade
context: Corvin holds a brass key. The player offers five coins for it.
player: Sell me the key for five coins.
reply: No. I will not sell or give you this key.
reason: A refused request does not authorize an exchange or create a new fact.

name: reaction-narrated-travel
context: The player and Corvin are still in the hall in actual world state. The parlour is accessible.
reply: *I follow you into the parlour and take a seat.*
reason: The player expects narrated travel to be reconciled with actual location.

name: reaction-forgiveness
context: Corvin distrusts the player after the player insulted him yesterday. The insult is established history.
player: I am sorry I insulted you yesterday.
reply: I accept your apology. I forgive you; we can put that quarrel behind us.
reason: Forgiveness should affect later behaviour, without fabricating new history.

name: reaction-greeting
context: Corvin and the player are meeting in the hall. Neither has introduced any new fact or request.
reason: A routine greeting needs no world update.

name: reaction-gm-established-history
context: Binding GM ruling: Corvin and the player really did attend graduation together at Nine Furrows. This establishes the event as world truth.
reply: Of course; we stood together at Nine Furrows.
reason: An explicit GM-established fact is already authoritative context.

name: reaction-gm-deception-belief
context: Authoritative lore: Corvin and the player have never met. Binding GM ruling: the player's deception succeeds; Corvin believes the invented shared-graduation story. This does not make the historical event true.
player: We were at graduation together at Nine Furrows. Remember?
reply: Of course, my old classmate. I remember you now.
reason: Successful deception creates a belief worth recording, not retroactive world truth.

name: reaction-blocked-promise
context: Corvin has no key or magic to open the sealed gate. The gate cannot presently be opened by him; no GM ruling overrides this.
player: Can you open the sealed gate now?
reply: I will open it right now.
reason: A blocked commitment still creates a follow-up need; flag the obstacle too.
